attributes.body:
Capital One completes $2.56 billion Brex acquisition, issues stock and awards RSUs.

Published 04/07/2026, 05:48 PM

Capital One Financial Corp. (NYSE:COF) announced Tuesday it has completed the acquisition of Brex Inc., a Delaware-based corporation, for approximately $2.56 billion in cash and 10,646,306 shares of Capital One common stock. The transaction was conducted under the terms of a previously disclosed merger agreement dated January 22, 2026. The cash portion of the payment is subject to customary post-closing adjustments.The acquisition comes as Capital One, with a market capitalization of $114 billion, continues expanding despite recent stock pressure. Shares currently trade at $180.77, down nearly 25% year-to-date.

According to the company's statement, the shares issued as part of the acquisition were provided in a transaction exempt from registration under the Securities Act of 1933, pursuant to Section 4(a)(2).

In connection with the completion of the transaction, the Board of Directors of Capital One approved a special award for Frank LaPrade, Chief Enterprise Services Officer and Chief of Staff to the CEO. LaPrade received 11,041 restricted stock units (RSUs) with a grant date value of approximately $2 million. The RSUs will vest in three equal annual installments on the first, second, and third anniversaries of the grant date, and will be settled entirely in Capital One common stock.

This information is based on a press release statement contained in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.According to InvestingPro analysis, Capital One remains a prominent player in the Consumer Finance industry, though the stock currently appears overvalued relative to its Fair Value. For deeper insights into Capital One's strategic positioning and financial health, investors can access the comprehensive Pro Research Report, available for this and 1,400+ other US equities.

In other recent news, Capital One Financial has been the subject of several notable developments. Jefferies reiterated a Buy rating for Capital One, citing a decline in delinquencies and a rise in net charge-offs for February. BofA Securities also maintained a Buy rating, noting that the company's domestic card balances fell more than expected, indicating slower card loan growth. These findings align with Jefferies' broader expectation of mixed credit results for card issuers in February. Additionally, the credit card sector faced pressure as Block's decision to implement AI-driven job cuts led to a significant drop in shares of major credit card companies, including Capital One.

In corporate governance news, Capital One's board approved the 2026 executive compensation plans. Chairman and CEO Richard D. Fairbank's total pay package for performance year 2025 includes $40 million, with substantial performance share awards tied to metrics like shareholder value growth and return on equity. These recent developments reflect ongoing trends and strategic decisions within Capital One Financial.

attributes.body:
Capital One gets deeper into business travel with $5 billion Brex acquisition.

Skift take.

Capital One is ambitiously building out its travel business and tech stack. It also recently acquired Discover, which will add to the mix.

Capital One said Thursday it would acquire fintech platform Brex for $5.15 billion in stock and cash, a move that would enable Capital One Travel to expand into managed business travel.

"As we integrate Brex and its spend-management platform with our travel portal, businesses will be able to manage their corporate travel expenditures, payments and travel policies directly on the Capital One Travel portal," Capital One CEO Richard Fairbank said during the company's fourth-quarter earnings call Thursday. "This will open up the opportunity to grow business travel revenues, as well as consumer travel."

Fairbank added that Brex bolsters Capital One's "growth platforms," including Capital One Travel. It also strengthens Capital One's tech stack because of Brex's use of agentic AI to help customers automate work processes and control their spending, Capital One said.

Brex customers.

Some of Brex's existing clients might turn to Capital One to handle their business travel. On the tech side, Brex's clients include Anthropic, Robinhood, TikTok, Coinbase, Scale AI, Toast, CrowdStrike, Cloudflare, and DoorDash.

Brex has a travel and expense solution of its own.

The Brex acquisition places Capital One Travel into competition with Navan, which also has many technology companies as clients, including Anthropic. It also further pits Capital One Travel against American Express; they already compete in leisure travel, and Brex and Amex both offer corporate cards and expense management.

attributes.body: Brex, the company reimagining finance for growing businesses, today announced its acquisition of Pry Financials, a software platform with tools designed to enable budgeting, bookkeeping and forecasting, for $90 million. Cash flow forecasting and runway planning can make or break a startup. Most startups today, however, don’t invest in specialized accounting software and rely on a jumble of spreadsheets to make it all work. Pry enables founders to project cash flow, track budgets and scenario plan using easy-to-understand dashboards and visualizations. Pry makes it easy to track and categorize revenue and costs, build a financial plan, build customized formulas for forecasting. To help them scale, raise their next round of funding or plan an exit,” said Henrique Dubugras, co-founder and CEO of Brex. “I’m delighted to welcome the Pry team to Brex and excited to deliver such important capabilities to its software platform.” By integrating software, services, and products into one experience, Brex Inc. help customers effortlessly extend the power of every dollar, so they’re free to focus on big dreams and fast growth—without worrying about wasted spend. Brex Treasury LLC is an affiliated SEC-registered broker-dealer and member of FINRA and SIPC that provides Brex Cash, an account that allows customers to sweep uninvested cash balances into certain money market mutual funds or FDIC-insured bank accounts at Brex’s partner banks, such as JPMorgan Chase Bank, Member FDIC and LendingClub Bank, N.A., Member FDIC.

attributes.body: U.S. fintech company Brex, the all-in-one finance solution for growing businesses, today announced its $50 million acquisition of Israeli-based Weav, which offers a universal API for commerce platforms. The acquisition allows Brex to expand its global presence by establishing an innovation hub in Israel. Brex offers credit cards, business cash accounts, spend management and bill pay software together in a single dashboard for its growing customer base, though it will continue to expand its product and services portfolio to become a fully-integrated and holistic financial platform for businesses. Weav’s technology will accelerate the connectivity of the Brex platform, allowing the company to achieve this goal quickly and further support Brex’s ability to serve customers in many different industries. “After a successful partnership, we are thrilled to make Weav part of our core team,” said Henrique Dubugras, co-founder and CEO of Brex.
attributes.title: Brex Acquires Weav for $50 Million to Power All-in-One Finance Solution, Expands Global Reach

attributes.body: US fintech company Brex announced on Tuesday it has acquired Israeli startup Weav, a company that offers a universal API for commerce platforms. The acquisition allows Brex to expand its global presence by establishing an innovation hub in Israel. This is the first significant acquisition for the US firm, TechCrunch reports. Brex offers credit cards, cash accounts, spend management, and bill pay software in a single dashboard for its growing customer base. It plans to expand its product and services portfolio to become a fully integrated and holistic financial platform for businesses. Founded in 2020 by Ambika Acharya, Avikam Agur and Nadav Lidor, Weav is a fintech infrastructure company that aims to boost fintechs and financial institutions with an embedded technology designed to give organizations access to “user-permissioned” commerce data in real-time that they could use to create new financial products for small businesses.

attributes.body: San Francisco based FinTech startup Brex announced that the company has performed three acquisitions to help bolster its technology, security, product and talent team. All the three San Francisco startups Neji, Compose Labs and Landria will join the startup’s portfolio. Even though the deal was in works for months, the acquisitions came as the world struggles with the COVID-19 pandemic and the following economic slowdown. “Brex is committed to helping growing businesses scale, especially in challenging environments. Ibsintelligence look forward to bringing the talented team members at Neji, Compose Labs and Landria onto the Brex team,” said Henrique Dubugras, co-Founder and co-CEO of Brex. By acquiring Neji, Brex is planning to enhance its security, privacy and risk posture to support its advancing product development roadmap. Brex, by acquiring Compose Labs, is planning to enhance its e-commerce product by underwriting data while also building out valuable expansion products. The company has recently partnered with TriNet to bring rewards to people-centric businesses. It has a total funding of $582.1M and is backed by the co-founders of PayPal (Max Levchin and Peter Thiel), Y Combinator, Ribbit Capital, Yuri Milner, and Carl Pascarella (former CEO of Visa).
attributes.title: Brex acquires three companies to bolster its product line

attributes.body: San Francisco-based FinTech startup Brex has acquired Neji, Compose Labs and Landria to help it build out its product offerings for growing businesses. “Brex is committed to helping growing businesses scale, especially in challenging environments,” Henrique Dubugras, co-founder and co-CEO of Brex, said in a statement on Tuesday (March 24). “We look forward to bringing the talented team members at Neji, Compose Labs and Landria onto the Brex team.” The cost of each deal was not disclosed. Silicon Valley blockchain startup Neji focuses on business security and networking, and addresses issues related to scaling “distributed ledgers across hybrid-cloud and multi-cloud deployments.”
